newsitem.title: GERMANY: Russian expert tells of drunken A-bomb theft.
newsitem.headline: Russian expert tells of drunken A-bomb theft.

text.p: A pair of drunken Russian workmen stole two atomic warheads from a factory as a prank in 1993, according to a Russian disarmament expert quoted by a German newspaper.

The expert, Vladimir Orlov, told a seminar in Bonn at the beginning of April that the theft -- done on a bet -- was the first time an actual nuclear weapon had been stolen, the Frankfurter Allgemeine Sunday newspaper reported.
Security forces traced the two missing warheads to a garage in a residential area, he said.
Orlov said the incident took place at "Factory X" east of the Urals in November 1993.
Since the breakup of the Soviet Union in 1991, Western governments have worried that material stolen in former Soviet bloc could put nuclear arms within reach of non-nuclear states.
The newspaper said Orlov was the head of the Moscow Institute for Security and Politics which it said had a good reputation among scientists outside Russia.
